decided_by: approved with 4 advisory objection(s) — none high-severity

objections.problem: Rationale asserts 'emitted output is unchanged' when moving the locked-component filter from SQL (`AND pc.locked_at IS NULL`) into the Go loop, but this is asserted rather than demonstrated by a diff-style test comparing old vs new emitted work items; a regression here would silently change which pages get findings filed.

The sketch shown for this edit uses a 2-arg signature `(pageID, scan)`, later revised by edits 6/7 to a 4-arg signature; this is explained via a 'SIGNATURE NOTE' but means edit 2 in isolation is not the shipped code — acceptable given the explanation, but makes the plan harder to verify edit-by-edit.

Most edits (1,2,3,5,7-partial,8-partial) are declared already 'shipped and running' rather than proposed; the plan is largely documenting existing code for review after the fact ('review follows the change here'). This is disclosed and grounded, but narrows what this review can actually gate to edits 6/7/8.

reviews.notes: All 8 edits make real changes (no pure audits/comments); each cited mechanism in the rationale (shared scan extraction, examined/skipped-locked counters, copy-changed gate, claim-granular gate, loader contract, coverage test) has a corresponding edit, and edit ordering is causally coherent (revalidator registration depends on the shared scan and the loader's CreatedAt column). The plan is large but the added safety gates are load-bearing given the factual-claim domain and prior council rounds' objections, so it is not obviously over-scoped. Main soft concern is that most edits are presented as already shipped, limiting how much this review can actually change; that is disclosed by the author rather than hidden.

objections.problem: 016b §9 case '093_HANDOFF_2026-07-26_stat_audit_has_one_guarded_call_site_rerender_unchecked' names exactly this shape in exactly this area (a stat/claims audit whose guard covers one call site while a rerender path stays unchecked). This plan's own grounded_in confirms scanStoredStatClaims (in check_unverified_claims_stats.go) is called only from inside the new ScanDeployedClaims, but does not check whether any rerender path (rerender_page_sections, rerender_single_page) independently re-derives or re-reads claims state outside this shared scan. Given the platform's history of exactly this asymmetry, the single-call-site claim needs to be checked against rerender code, not just against grep of current call sites.

Risk 7 in the plan itself admits voice_tells has the identical moving-standard hole and receives neither the copy-changed nor claim-granular gate -- this is the author self-identifying pattern (c) (one call site of a shared judgement gets the rigorous fix, the sibling stays heuristic; cf. 016b §9 'One call site of a shared judgement gets the rigorous fix; the sibling stays heuristic'). It is tracked in features_open/032 rather than hidden, which is the right response, but the router should know this is a known-recurring shape being deliberately deferred, not resolved.

missing: Whether any rerender/rebuild path (rerender_page_sections, rerender_single_page, page-content-writer) independently reads or re-derives claims_unverified state outside ScanDeployedClaims -- unresolved by the given grounded_in evidence, which only greps current call sites of scanStoredStatClaims, not all consumers of the claims mechanism.
reviews.notes: This plan is unusually well-defended against the core recurring pattern: it explicitly adds ComponentsExamined/ComponentsSkippedLocked/ExaminedTextBySlot precisely so 'read nothing' cannot masquerade as 'clean', and every unresolvable arm returns non-terminal 'unknown' rather than silently closing -- that is the proven fix shape from bugs_closed/032 (verifier treating a missing target as success) applied correctly. My objection is narrower: case 093's title matches this exact subsystem (stat/claims audit, guarded call site vs. unchecked rerender), and the plan's single-producer/single-call-site claim rests on a grep of current call sites rather than a check against rerender paths specifically. Not a veto-level concern given the extensive gating already built in, but worth one more check before merge given the title match is this precise.

objections.problem: claimStillOnPage / claim-granular gate is written as a claims_unverified-specific mechanism, but risk item 7 admits voice_tells has the identical moving-standard hole and will need the same shape. The plan already files features_open/032 to track building a shared helper later rather than now, which is reasonable, but there is a real risk a second bespoke gate gets written for voice_tells before that helper exists — worth the router flagging so the next revalidator addition is checked against this one first.

reviews.notes: This plan is a good example of the discipline working: it extracts the existing UnverifiedClaimsCheck emit-side scan into ScanDeployedClaims for reuse by the revalidator rather than writing a second copy of the predicate; it reuses the existing reviewRevalidators map/loadParkedReviewItems shared loader pattern already used by voice_tells etc rather than building a new drain path; it reuses datahelpers.ExtractAssertionText rather than a new extractor; and it explicitly measured single-producer status via code_symbols before proceeding (correcting an earlier round's wrong two-producer claim). content_rewrite was checked and rejected as a candidate mechanism on evidence. The only soft concern is the claim-granular gate being bespoke to this type when a structurally identical gate is already known to be needed for voice_tells — tracked as a future feature rather than solved now, which is acceptable but worth watching so it doesn't get re-invented per-type.

No schema DDL (no RENAME/DROP COLUMN) — the column-rename risk rule doesn't apply; edit 8 only ADDS a SELECT/scan field, consistent with the additive-first-then-optionally-drop pattern this rule prefers. No new site_work_items INSERT path is introduced (this is a revalidation/close pipeline reading and updating existing rows), so the idx_swi_dedup/DELETE+INSERT contract is not implicated. No workflow-step config or agent_definitions.input_contract is touched — the struct/column additions (ClaimsPageScan.NewestComponentUpdate/ExaminedTextBySlot, parkedReviewItem.CreatedAt) are internal Go/SQL plumbing within one action's own query, not a cross-agent input needing contract declaration, so DECLARED CONTRACTS doesn't apply either. The revalidator runs as a DB-scan step inside the existing review-queue sweep rather than spawning a pod; the plan's own grounded_in cites the voice_tells revalidator already running this same shape successfully post-roll, so this is precedent-consistent with WRAPPER-ORCHESTRATOR rather than a violation (a pure SQL scan is not the LLM/crawl/heavy-runtime work that rule targets). No guideline gap worth flagging.

objections.problem: The revalidator registration is done correctly via the reviewRevalidators registry map (no filename-convention resolution), and check_unverified_claims_stats.go is correctly identified as unregistered rather than assumed to be a second producer from its filename — this is the right use of the registry discipline. No objection to the mechanism itself.

missing: No doc_plans/doc_notes NOTES entry is added for this change's own design decisions (the two gates, the token-vs-snippet measurement, the risk-7 gap for voice_tells) under a subject_key for this check/revalidator — the submission instead tracks risk 7 in a markdown features_open file and cites doc_notes only for landmine-sync/council-report verification. If discovery_checks/revalidators are a subject_type this estate tracks in doc_plans/doc_notes (as tools/experience plans are), this decision history is not being left there for the next fixer; if that table is reserved for content/tool plans rather than backend Go mechanisms, this is moot — flagging for a human to confirm which convention applies here.
reviews.notes: The plan reuses shared extraction/scan functions (ScanDeployedClaims, LoadEvidenceBase, datahelpers.ExtractAssertionText) rather than reinventing context-gathering, wires the new revalidator through the existing registry map rather than by filename/action-key guessing, and explicitly verified via code_symbols that check_unverified_claims_stats.go registers no check before treating it as inert — good registry discipline, matching the platform's stated rule. It also transparently investigated cmd/bundle/contextkit, found it not wired into this module's build, and used the code_symbols index directly instead, which is the right fallback rather than silently skipping investigation. Only soft concern is the absence of a doc_notes/doc_plans entry documenting this subject's design decisions for the next fixer, which may or may not be the right convention for backend mechanism changes versus content/tool plans — left as a question for a human rather than an objection.

objections.problem: loadParkedReviewItems / parkedReviewItemColumns is the shared query serving all six covered item types in the review-queue-revalidate-daily sweep (unresolved_cta, required_fields_missing, needs_section_data, needs_page, voice_tells, now claims_unverified). Adding a column here is a scan-error class of failure, not a compile error — a mismatch takes down every revalidator in the sweep, not just this one. The plan itself flags this in risks and mitigates with TestParkedReviewItemSelectAndScanAgree, which is the right shape, but this is still the single highest-blast-radius edit in the plan and deserves to be called out as touching shared infrastructure rather than being folded silently into 'one map entry is the whole wiring.'

check_unverified_claims.go is the emit side of a discovery check run fleet-wide via the scheduled discovery-check dispatch (site-discovery-rotation-*). The extraction into ScanDeployedClaims/LoadEvidenceBase is claimed to leave emitted output byte-identical, but that claim rests on the refactor being purely mechanical — any behavioral drift here (e.g. the locked-component skip moving from SQL predicate to Go loop) changes what every future discovery run finds across the whole fleet, not just this feature. The plan asserts equivalence but I want it checked at the schema level for regression risk on existing open claims_unverified rows.

reviews.notes: No core orchestrator, Kafka/messaging, agent spawning, or agent_definitions workflow-JSON edits here — this stays within one scheduled action pipeline (review-queue-revalidate-daily) plus its upstream discovery check. Not an architecture-change signal: five files, one action package plus one discovery_checks file, exported types kept as aliases to minimize churn. The real containable risk is the shared loader (edit 8) and the fleet-scope of the discovery check (edit 1); both are already acknowledged by the author with tests and measured risk quantification, which is the right posture. Object rather than veto: the shared-column risk is real but mechanically guarded by a dedicated contract test, and no precedent in this council's history was surfaced against this exact site absent my checks returning.

This plan is about the review-queue sweep (site_work_items revalidation for claims_unverified), not the diagnosis loop (090_TRIGGER, diagnose_* actions, diagnosis_artifacts, read-only SQL data_requests, error_step config). None of the seven edits touch platform/orchestration/actions/diagnose_*.go, sqlguard, the diagnose-agent pod isolation, or diagnosis_artifacts persistence. The verdict ladder, gates, and evidence citations described here belong to a distinct HITL revalidation mechanism with its own cite-based conventions (evidence includes filedAt/newest_component_update), which superficially resembles the diagnosis loop's discipline but is a different subsystem entirely. Out of scope for this seat.

This plan touches the review-queue revalidation sweep (revalidate_review_queue_action.go / reviewRevalidators map), not the audit->fix->re-audit pass-cap/lock machinery. claims_unverified is a HITL-terminal discovery-check finding with no handler_agent by design; this change adds a revalidator that re-runs the SAME scan predicate the emit-side check already uses (ScanDeployedClaims), scoped optionally to a single page, mirroring the already-shipped voice_tells revalidator pattern cited as precedent. No pass-cap bypass, no auto-unlock, no re-audit of locked sections (locked_at here is the human-pin skip already honored by the original check, now counted rather than silently dropped — still skipped, never re-read or unlocked). No new discovery check is enabled and no check inserts its own work items; Run still appends WorkItemSpecs unchanged, and the revalidator only updates/closes existing parked rows via the runner's existing revalidation path, not fresh inserts. Verification is a targeted scan, not a fleet re-audit. The shared max_items cap across revalidator types (a known landmine) is addressed with live cap_binding=false headroom (14% of cap). No depends_on or dispatch-concurrency changes. Approve.

This is squarely a truth-of-claims mechanism, so it gets full scrutiny, but the design is the right shape: retraction never edits copy and never dispatches a rewrite, it only withdraws a stale finding, and closure requires BOTH (1) the page having demonstrably changed since filing and (2) the specific cited text being gone from its own slot — not merely the register moving. That directly answers the poisoned-spec and register-authority risks this seat exists for, and the token-vs-snippet measurement (18/41 vs 40/41 sensitivity) is a real, checked design choice rather than an assumption. Every failure mode returns 'unknown' (non-terminal, human still sees it), which is the correct safe direction for a factual-claims gate. Residual exposure is named honestly in risks: ~2/18 false refusals, HITL-terminal semantics being overridden by automation, and voice_tells left uncovered by the stronger gate (tracked as a feature, not silently accepted). No prompts/specs are altered to instruct content generation, no banned_claims list or scanner is weakened, and no disclaimer/legal surface is touched. Nothing here creates or emits a new user-facing claim; it only ever removes a work-item record about a claim that can no longer be found. Approve, with the request that risk item 3 (whether the claim-check should replace rather than merely supplement the timestamp gate) actually gets an owner decision rather than staying open indefinitely, since as currently ANDed a genuinely-fixed page with an unbumped updated_at will incorrectly stay parked — annoying but safe, not a content-integrity fault.

This change is confined to discovery-check scanning and the review-queue revalidation sweep — it reads page_components/content_data via ScanDeployedClaims and compares timestamps/text, but never writes rendered_html, content_data, or component templates, and never dispatches a rerender or assemble action. No render path is added; retraction only closes a site_work_items row. The locked-component move from SQL to Go preserves the same skip semantics (pinned content still excluded from findings), just counted rather than silently dropped, which is consistent with the fail-loud posture. No chrome/header/footer routing, no data-runtime-fill interaction, no CSS/var() touch, and no reliance on a plain page-rerender as proof of anything — the deploy verification cited is a pod-binary digest check, not a rerender completion claim. Out of scope for this reviewer's contracts.

objections.problem: The claim-granular and copy-changed gates both judge the DB's stored page_components.content_data/rendered_html as ground truth for closing a human-review item, but per the documented landmine 'page_components.content_data / rendered_html -- a data repair RACES the sweep that publishes it — and the DB is not the website', a component can be updated in the DB (bumping updated_at, changing ExaminedTextBySlot) before the corresponding rerender/deploy has actually shipped the change to the served page. The plan verifies its own deploy via /proc/1/exe (correct discipline) but never checks whether the PAGE being revalidated has actually deployed since its content_data changed -- pages.build_status / deployed_at is not consulted anywhere in the gate. A closed claims_unverified item could therefore certify a claim as 'removed' while the live site still serves the old text.

reviews.notes: No raw SQL production-data surgery here -- this is Go application code reading/writing site_work_items through normal action paths, so needle-gate discipline (backups, counted needles, guarded idempotent UPDATE) is largely N/A. Blast-radius scoping is handled well: the plan explicitly enumerates page status (active/archived/deleted) rather than assuming an informational column, and quantifies the 2-of-23 exposure on non-live pages. Deploy verification follows the correct lore exactly: /proc/1/exe grep with exit-code capture, image-digest cross-check across all 41 pods, and a pre-change baseline -- textbook 'verify against the running pod'. No stored-template Mode A/B repair-vs-regenerate concern (not touching html_template). The one real gap is the DB-vs-website race noted above: both gates trust page_components state as proof the copy changed, with no check that the page has actually redeployed since. Given the safe-direction design (wrong verdict -> unknown, not resolved) this is a real but bounded risk, not a blocker.

Root cause addressed: a genuinely unwired item_type (no handler, no revalidator) gets one, not a patch around a symptom. The moving-standard risk (register edits mimicking fixes) is explicitly gated by two ANDed checks rather than silently ignored, and the plan states the residual gaps (rephrased claims, voice_tells left uncovered) as tracked deferrals rather than hiding them. Reuse is respected: ScanDeployedClaims/LoadEvidenceBase are extracted for reuse by both emit and revalidate paths instead of duplicating the query; the revalidator slots into the existing reviewRevalidators map pattern. ClaimFinding is an explicit, justified type alias, not a silent rename. Sketches show parameterized queries ($1/$2), consistent with schema-first discipline. Tone is plain and mechanism-focused throughout.

This is a review-queue drain for a content-governance work item type (unsupported factual claims). It does not touch classification, revenue-model shaping, or site-type direction. It doesn't let downstream agents override the classifier's spec — it's a truth/evidence retraction gate for prose claims, not a spec-implementation shortcut. The two ANDed gates (copy changed since filing + cited text gone from its slot) are conservative and default to non-terminal 'unknown', which is the correct failure direction and consistent with the platform's stated aversion to silent override — if anything this pattern (mark, surface, never silently resolve) mirrors the mission's anti-silent-override principle applied to the review queue itself. Mission-neutral.

objections.problem: The load-bearing correction from round 1 ('there is one producer, not two') rests entirely on a self-reported code_symbols query and a self-reported `grep` result for check_unverified_claims_stats.go having no init()/WorkItemSpec. This is exactly the class of claim this seat exists to check independently rather than accept from the submission's own measurements section — especially since a wrong answer here revives the co-dedup'd-producer landmine (adopting a revalidator can close the OTHER producer's finding).

Author states ScanDeployedClaims, LoadEvidenceBase, ClaimsPageScan and the reviewRevalidators['claims_unverified'] wiring are 'Shipped and running, verified at HEAD' via a pod-grep/proc-1-exe probe and code_symbols. Neither the pod nor code_symbols freshness is checkable from this schema-only seat; this claim about a running binary cannot be settled here and must not be treated as established without the named independent check.

missing: Whether check_unverified_claims_stats.go emits any site_work_items row with item_type='claims_unverified' at runtime (init-less/registration-less code can still be reachable via a shared call path the symbol search would not surface as a 'producer').
reviews.notes: This submission is unusual for this seat: most absence claims run the other direction from usual (it argues code already exists rather than that it's missing), and the plan explicitly separates shipped-at-HEAD from committed-not-rolled edits. That discipline is good, but the two load-bearing existence claims underneath it (single producer; already-shipped symbols) are asserted from the author's own out-of-schema measurements (code_symbols query results, pod grep) rather than anything checkable from the SQL schema here. Given this has already been through several council rounds on other seats' objections, I am not flagging this high, but the single-producer correction specifically changes the applicability of a known co-dedup landmine and deserves an independent code_symbols check before being taken as settled.

objections.problem: loadParkedReviewItems is shared by all six covered item types; a SELECT/Scan mismatch fails every revalidator in the sweep at once. This is real blast radius, but it is mitigated by TestParkedReviewItemSelectAndScanAgree and is the correct place to add the column rather than a parallel query, so it is a low-severity note, not an architecture objection.

reviews.notes:
ARCHITECTURE_SIGNAL: point_fix | DEFLECTIONS: unknown

The extension point here (reviewRevalidators map + shared ScanDeployedClaims/loadParkedReviewItems) is the platform's own designed mechanism for adding a revalidator, and this plan uses it exactly as designed — one map entry, one shared scan reused by both emit and revalidate sides, one additive column on a loader already shared by six item types. No new contract, no new wire shape, no cross-package coordination beyond the four files that already constitute this subsystem. That is a point fix riding an existing, working architecture, not a new mechanism smuggled in through a bug patch.

Forward fitness: the future load is 'more revalidators for more item_types', and the pattern (extract shared scan, gate on copy-changed evidence, unit-test the verdict ladder as a pure function) generalises cleanly — risk 7 already names voice_tells as the next candidate and defers it rather than forcing it in here, which is the right discipline.

One thing worth flagging as insufficient rather than as this plan's fault: there is no generic 'moving-standard' gate abstraction, so each revalidator (voice_tells now, claims_unverified here) reimplements its own version of 'did the copy change vs did the standard change'. Two instances is not yet a trigger, but a third bespoke copy would be the point to extract a shared gate helper rather than a third parallel ladder. Not blocking here.
